newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds frozen in tight range before FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Bunds frozen in tight range before FOMC.

text.p: German Bunds were firm but frozen in a tight range in late trade on Tuesday, as dealers were unwilling to enter new positions ahead of the outcome of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting.

Most analysts expect a 25 basis-point rise in the Federal Funds rate to 5.50 percent and dealers said this was already factored into the market. The German debt market is likely to be closed by the time the Fed announces its decision.
June Bund futures were trading at 100.32 at 1515 GMT, up 0.19 points from Monday's close, after moving in a narrow 16 basis-point range all day.
Dealers said a decision to keep U.S. rates unchanged, or a 50 basis-point rise in the Fed Funds rate, would probably hit U.S. Treasury prices and cause Bunds to fall in their wake.
Bunds rose early in the session on the back of tame regional inflation data.

Economists said March consumer inflation data from the states of North Rhine-Westphalia, Hesse and Baden-Wuerttemberg were lower than expected and allayed fears of an inflation rise sparked by strong price gains in January and February.
The three states all reported modest month-on-month declines of 0.1 or 0.2 percent in their consumer price indices.
The year-on-year inflation rates slowed to 1.4 percent in Hesse and Baden-Wuerttemberg and to 1.8 percent in North-Rhine Westphalia.

Data from those states and from Bavaria are used to calculate preliminary west German consumer prices which economists expected to be flat or down 0.1 percent month-on-month and up 1.6 percent year-on-year.
Bavaria has yet to report its price data.
Those figures helped offset news of a strong 0.5 percent rise in German import prices in February month-on-month. The year-on-year rise was 3.0 percent.

Economists said the import price rise, although above expectations for a rise of 0.3 percent, was not surprising since it referred to February and reflected the increase in the dollar and in oil prices.
